Buyer & tenant journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it.

01

Discover and enquire

Buyers, tenants, members and project owners find a project, space or builder through portals, ads, partners, hoardings, referrals and tenders, and expect a useful reply within minutes, often on WhatsApp and often after office hours.

Touchpoints

  • Property portals such as 99acres, MagicBricks and Housing.com
  • Meta and Google lead forms and the website
  • Channel partner client registrations
  • Hoardings, site boards and missed-call numbers
  • RFQs and tender notices

Accountable owner

Pre-sales head, channel partner manager or bid manager

Automations on this stage

Discover and enquire · 3–5 weeks

Portal and ad lead capture with fast response and qualification

Enquiries from property portals, Meta and Google lead forms, the website and missed-call numbers reach one CRM queue within minutes, are deduplicated and answered with approved project content, then qualified and assigned to an executive with response-time alerts.

View the blueprint ↗Discover and enquire · 4–6 weeks

Channel partner client registration with duplicate and conflict checks

Partners register clients through a simple portal or WhatsApp form before a visit. Each registration is checked against existing leads and other partners, timestamped, confirmed with a validity period and linked to the visit, so attribution rests on evidence rather than memory.

View the blueprint ↗Discover and enquire · 4–6 weeks

RFQ and BOQ intake with extraction, vendor quotes and bid tracking

Tender and RFQ emails become entries in a bid register. AI extracts BOQ line items from spreadsheets and PDFs into a structured sheet mapped to your rate library and flags missing specifications, and the team tracks quotes, clarifications and deadlines until the estimator signs off.

View the blueprint ↗
02

Visit and evaluate

Prospects see the site, sample flat or center in person or by video, compare options and costs, and bring family members, partners or brokers into the decision.

Touchpoints

  • Site and sample flat visits
  • Video site visits for buyers abroad
  • Co-working and office tours
  • Cost sheets and proposals

Accountable owner

Sales manager, NRI desk lead or center manager

Automations on this stage

Visit and evaluate · 3–4 weeks

Site visit booking, reminders, check-in and post-visit follow-up

Qualified buyers book a site visit on WhatsApp against sales gallery capacity, receive reminders with the location pin, check in by QR code on arrival and get a feedback request afterwards, while the executive's notes become a confirmed CRM summary and next step.

View the blueprint ↗Visit and evaluate · 3–5 weeks

NRI buyer nurturing across time zones with video site visits

Buyers abroad get replies and updates in their own daytime, book video site visits that overlap with Indian working hours, and receive answers on eligibility, payments and documentation only from content your legal team approves, with an NRI desk manager owning every relationship.

View the blueprint ↗Visit and evaluate · 4–6 weeks

Office and co-working enquiries from tour to signed agreement

Enquiries for desks, cabins or office floors are qualified, matched to live inventory, booked into a center tour and followed by a proposal from the approved price book. New members and tenants are onboarded with company KYC, access and billing set up from one record.

View the blueprint ↗
03

Book, document and finance

The buyer or occupier commits: booking amount, KYC, allotment letter, agreement for sale and its registration, home-loan sanction, lease or membership signing, and brokerage for the partner who introduced them.

Touchpoints

  • Booking form and booking amount
  • KYC and allotment letter
  • Agreement for sale and registration
  • Home-loan sanction
  • Lease or membership agreement
  • Brokerage statement and invoice

Accountable owner

CRM head, legal team and finance controller

Automations on this stage

Book, document and finance · 6–8 weeks

Booking to registered agreement: KYC, allotment and home loans

After a booking, buyers complete a secure application with KYC, the CRM team verifies it, allotment letters and agreement drafts come from legal-approved templates, demands stay within the RERA advance limit until registration, and each home-loan case is tracked with the buyer's lender.

View the blueprint ↗Book, document and finance · 4–5 weeks

Client KYC and PMLA record-keeping for brokerages

As a deal moves toward closure, the brokerage collects client KYC through a secure link, records beneficial ownership and payment details, screens names against the lists its AML policy requires and keeps a five-year record. Possible red flags go privately to the Principal Officer.

View the blueprint ↗Book, document and finance · 4–6 weeks

Brokerage eligibility, invoicing and payout tracking

Every deal's brokerage terms, milestones, invoices and payments sit on one record. Developers and landlords see which partner claims are due and approve them; brokerages see what each developer owes them and how commissions split among their agents.

View the blueprint ↗
04

Build and pay

Construction moves through certified stages while buyers pay milestone demands, lenders disburse, and site teams manage progress, labor, materials and safety every day.

Touchpoints

  • Progress updates with photos
  • Milestone demand letters and reminders
  • Home-loan disbursements
  • Daily site reports and material requests
  • Safety and near-miss reports

Accountable owner

Project head with the finance controller

Automations on this stage

Build and pay · 5–7 weeks

Construction progress updates and milestone-linked demand letters

When the project's architect or engineer certifies a construction stage, buyers receive a progress update with photos and a demand letter calculated from their payment plan, once finance approves the batch. Lenders get disbursement requests for loan buyers, and monthly updates fill the gaps.

View the blueprint ↗Build and pay · 5–8 weeks

Daily site reports, labor attendance and material approvals

Site engineers file one mobile daily report covering work done against plan, photos, manpower by subcontractor, equipment, materials received and material requests. Attendance is reconciled, requests are checked against BOQ balance and routed by value, and managers get a daily digest.

View the blueprint ↗Build and pay · 3–5 weeks

Safety incident and near-miss logging with immediate escalation

Anyone on site can report an injury, dangerous occurrence or near miss by WhatsApp or QR code, with photos. Serious events trigger immediate calls to the safety officer and project head, corrective actions are tracked, and statutory notices are drafted for the responsible person to file.

View the blueprint ↗
05

Possession and move-in

Once the occupancy certificate or fit-out completion is in hand, buyers and tenants clear final dues, inspect the space, raise snags and take possession or move in.

Touchpoints

  • Possession offer and final dues statement
  • Handover slot booking
  • Snag inspection and rectification
  • Key and access handover

Accountable owner

CRM handover manager and quality engineer

Automations on this stage

Possession and move-in · 4–6 weeks

Possession, fit-out handover and snag-list management

After the occupancy certificate or fit-out completion, buyers and tenants book handover slots, receive a final dues statement, report snags room by room with photos and track each item as the contractor fixes it and a quality engineer verifies it. Later defect reports follow the same path.

View the blueprint ↗
06

Occupy, renew and refer

Owners and tenants live with the space: rent and escalations, renewals and exits, maintenance and defect reports, and referrals to friends and colleagues.

Touchpoints

  • Rent invoices and reminders
  • Escalation and renewal notices
  • Maintenance and defect tickets
  • Referrals and reviews

Accountable owner

Asset manager, facility head or CRM head

Automations on this stage

Occupy, renew and refer · 4–6 weeks

Lease abstraction, rent, escalation and renewal reminders

Key dates and terms are extracted from signed leases and verified by the leasing manager. Rent invoices and reminders follow the lease calendar, escalations are calculated for finance to approve, and renewal and lock-in dates reach the asset manager early enough to act.

View the blueprint ↗

Where people stay in control

Human checkpoints across the journey.

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Portal and ad lead capture with fast response and qualificationDiscover and enquireThe assigned executive owns every qualified conversation and makes the first call where there is no WhatsApp opt-in. Prices come only from the approved price sheet; offers, discounts, payment-plan changes and possession dates go to the executive or sales manager. Marketing and legal approve all templates.
Channel partner client registration with duplicate and conflict checksDiscover and enquireThe channel partner manager decides every flagged duplicate or conflict under the written partner policy, and the sales head hears appeals. The automation never rejects a disputed claim on its own, and partners see only their own registrations.
RFQ and BOQ intake with extraction, vendor quotes and bid trackingDiscover and enquireThe chief estimator reviews every extracted line against the source document and approves every rate; extraction stays a draft until checked. A director approves the go or no-go decision, the margin and the final submission.
Site visit booking, reminders, check-in and post-visit follow-upVisit and evaluateExecutives confirm every AI visit summary before it enters the CRM and choose what follow-up content is sent. Cost sheets are generated only from the approved price sheet, and the sales manager reviews hot leads and any negotiation every day.
NRI buyer nurturing across time zones with video site visitsVisit and evaluateThe NRI desk relationship manager owns each buyer and handles every pricing, booking and documentation conversation. Legal approves the FAQ and the power of attorney guidance, and no automated message gives tax or foreign exchange advice on an individual case.
Office and co-working enquiries from tour to signed agreementVisit and evaluateCommunity and leasing managers run every tour and negotiation. Discounts outside the approved band need the center head, and lease terms, letters of intent and enterprise agreements are approved by the leasing director and legal before signature.
Booking to registered agreement: KYC, allotment and home loansBook, document and financeThe CRM team verifies every KYC file and legal approves every allotment letter and agreement. Any deviation in price, payment plan or terms needs the sales head and finance controller. Lenders decide loans, and nothing is shared with a lender without the buyer's consent.
Client KYC and PMLA record-keeping for brokeragesBook, document and financeThe Principal Officer reviews every flag and decides whether a report is required; the automation never files with FIU-IND and never contacts the client about a flag. The Designated Director approves the AML policy and screening lists, and the brokerage's legal advisers confirm thresholds and duties.
Brokerage eligibility, invoicing and payout trackingBook, document and financeThe finance controller approves every payout and every clawback, and the sales or leasing head approves any slab exception. The automation calculates, checks and reminds; it never releases money.
Construction progress updates and milestone-linked demand lettersBuild and payNo demand goes out without the architect's or engineer's certificate, the project head's approval and the finance controller's batch approval. Interest, waivers and payment-plan changes are decided by finance and the CRM head, and the project head approves every progress statement.
Daily site reports, labor attendance and material approvalsBuild and payThe project manager reviews the daily digest and approves material requests within their limit; the purchase head approves higher values and the quantity surveyor approves anything above BOQ balance. Subcontractor bills are certified by the project manager and accounts, not by the automation.
Safety incident and near-miss logging with immediate escalationBuild and payThe site safety officer owns every report and decides severity, investigation and closure; first aid, medical care and emergency response never wait for the automation. The safety officer or employer files statutory notices, and the system only drafts and reminds. The project head reviews serious incidents that day.
Possession, fit-out handover and snag-list managementPossession and move-inThe quality engineer verifies every closure and the CRM handover manager signs off each possession. Disputed snags, compensation questions and any structural concern go to the project head and, where needed, the structural consultant.
Lease abstraction, rent, escalation and renewal remindersOccupy, renew and referThe leasing manager verifies every abstract before any date is used. Finance approves escalation letters and invoices, legal approves notices, and the asset manager decides renewal terms and any rent concession.
